name: Muong Hoa valley
summary: Terrace valley 8 km southeast: look across the stepped fields and roofs for the picture under the ridge. Giay rice fills the narrow valley, and Mong and Dao fields sit higher on the slopes. A stream of about 15 km passes Lao Chai, Ta Van, Hau Thao, and Ban Ho. Harvest dates in print run from mid-August into November.
getThere: About 8 km southeast, at Hầu Thào. Minutes from the church are Check on arrival.
heroCaption: Stepped fields, roofs, and the valley at Muong Hoa
body: Muong Hoa is the farmed valley under the town, at Hầu Thào, 8 km southeast. You look across the terraces from mid-slope, or you walk them. Giay wet rice sits in the narrow valley. Mong and Dao fields sit higher up. The stream is about 15 km, with 22 tributaries, and it passes Lao Chai, Ta Van, Hau Thao, and Ban Ho. That stream is the lower section of Silver Waterfall.

Harvest dates span mid-August into November. The valley feature describes September rice as bright yellow. The Vietnam Tourism rice page puts the window at mid-August until early September. A Ta Van feature puts ripe rice at about mid-August to October. The Sa Pa page says September–October, and its chip says Sep–Nov. Plan for that whole span.
The Muong Hoa train is a separate ride of about 2 km toward the cable-car station, opened on 31 March 2018. The valley walk is the fields. Village gates along the road have their own fees.

gettingThere: The valley sits about 8 km southeast of the church, at Hầu Thào. The valley feature describes a high pass, then the fields. From July 2025 the old xã Mường Hoa sits inside xã Tả Van. A published minute count from the square is missing, so ask when you set out.

legs.heading: From the stone church
legs.body: Go southeast toward Hầu Thào, about 8 km. The valley feature describes a high pass before the fields.

admissionNote: A single valley ticket is unpublished. Gates at Lao Chai–Ta Van, Ta Phin, and Ban Ho have their own figures on the village pages. The Muong Hoa train fare is separate.
